akunleyan_payload.title: Àkúnlẹ̀yàn
akunleyan_payload.description: The sacred cosmological reality of the personal destiny chosen by the soul while kneeling before Olódùmarè in the heavenly realm (Ọ̀run) prior to physical incarnation on earth (Ayé).
akunleyan_payload.historical_timeline: Dating to antiquity and the primordial epoch of Ilé-Ifẹ̀, where Yorùbá metaphysical cosmology first formulated the tripartite doctrine of human destiny (Àkúnlẹ̀yàn, Àkúnlẹ̀gbà, Àyànmọ́). Documented exhaustively in classical Ifá liturgical chapters—most notably in Ògúndá Méjì, Ọ̀yẹ̀kú Méjì, and Èjì Ogbè—where the soul visits the house of Àjàlá Mọ̀pín (the cosmic potter who molds heads from clay) to select its Orí before kneeling before the Creator. Throughout 19th-century oral poetry and across Transatlantic Lucumí and Candomblé traditions, the concept of Àkúnlẹ̀yàn has provided the philosophical explanation for individual personality, gifts, and earthly vocations.
akunleyan_payload.etymology_and_philosophy: A compound metaphysical noun derived from 'À' (nominal prefix: that which) + 'kúnlẹ̀' (kneel upon the ground) + 'yàn' (to select or choose), literally signifying 'That which was chosen on bended knee'. In Yorùbá philosophy, kneeling (Ìkúnlẹ̀) is the ultimate posture of humility, reverence, and existential covenant before the Divine. Àkúnlẹ̀yàn affirms that human existence is not a product of blind chance or mechanical fate; every human being is an autonomous moral agent who voluntarily selected their life's purpose and spiritual portion. However, this celestial choice is forgotten at the threshold of physical birth (Oníbode Ọ̀run), necessitating the consultation of Ifá divination to decode one's original pre-natal covenant.
akunleyan_payload.material_and_craftsmanship: Materialized ritualistically through Ifá divination trays (Ọpọ́n Ifá) and sacred palm nuts (Ikin Ifá), which serve as the cosmic instruments through which a diviner (Babaláwo) reads the forgotten blueprint of an individual's Àkúnlẹ̀yàn. In personal shrines, it is honored through the consecration of the Ilé-Orí (cowrie-encrusted container of destiny).
akunleyan_payload.social_and_ritual_context: Invoked during the traditional naming ceremony (Ikọ́mọjá / Ìsọmọlórúkọ) on the 8th day, when the diviner performs the Esèntáyé ('Stepping into the World') rite to divine the child's Àkúnlẹ̀yàn and instruct parents on the taboos (Èèwọ̀) and professions aligned with the child's chosen path. In civil disputes, it inspires empathy and tolerance: recognizing that each person walks a unique path chosen in heaven.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Àkúnlẹ̀yàn ni àdáyébá; a dé ayé tán, ojú ń kán gbogbo wa. (That which was chosen kneeling in heaven is what we meet on earth; but having arrived in the physical world, we become impatient.)
A kì í kúnlẹ̀ yan èrò kan, kí a wá dé ayé tọ́jọ́ kọ́. (One does not kneel down in heaven to choose one destiny, only to arrive on earth and covet another's portion.)
Orí tí ó kúnlẹ̀ yan ọlá, kì í fẹsẹ̀ rìn nígbà tí àkókò rẹ̀ bá pé. (The head that knelt to choose sovereign honor will not walk in misery when its appointed season arrives.)
akunleyan_payload.diaspora_connections: Preserved intact within Cuban Lucumí and Brazilian Candomblé as the spiritual bedrock of divination rites (Itá). In the Lucumí 'Plante de Ifá' and 'Mano de Orula', the initiate's Odù is interpreted as the direct revelation of the Àkúnlẹ̀yàn made before Olodumare.
akunleyan_payload.cinematic_and_media_production: Visual staging should emphasize dreamlike, luminous aesthetics: soft celestial white light, shadows of a kneeling figure in pristine white robes before an ancient, benevolent silhouette, dissolving into the gentle earthy tones of a newborn baby's naming feast. Audio should incorporate the rhythmic, whispering cadence of Ikin nuts clicking together in a diviner's hands.

sensory_aesthetics.tactile: Cool white chalk (Ẹfun) marked on the forehead; smooth polished sacred Ikin palm nuts.
sensory_aesthetics.auditory: Gentle, resonant murmur of Ifá divination chants recited at dawn.
sensory_aesthetics.visual: A serene, contemplative kneeling figure bathed in golden morning light.

akunleyan_payload.sacred_exclusion_awo: Exoteric philosophy of destiny and ethical responsibility fully accessible. Secret initiatory chants for head-washing (Wíwẹ̀ Orí) remain within priesthood custody.
akunleyan_payload.provenance_and_citations: Wándé Abímbọ́lá (1976), Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus, Ibadan: Oxford University Press Nigeria; E. Bọ́lájì Ìdòwú (1962), Olódùmarè: God in Yoruba Belief, Longmans; Babatunde Lawal (1996), The Gẹ̀lẹ̀dẹ́ Spectacle, University of Washington Press; Rowland Abiodun (2014), Yoruba Art and Language, Cambridge University Press.

akunlegba_payload.title: Àkúnlẹ̀gbà
akunlegba_payload.description: The metaphysical portion of human destiny that is received or conferred by celestial authorities while the soul kneels in the presence of Olódùmarè, encompassing ancestral traits, physical constitution, and natural limitations.
akunlegba_payload.historical_timeline: Codified in classical Yorùbá philosophy alongside Àkúnlẹ̀yàn since antiquity. While Àkúnlẹ̀yàn emphasizes active choice, Àkúnlẹ̀gbà addresses inherited capacity, genetic lineage, and the cosmic parameters assigned to the individual by the Irúnmọlẹ̀. Detailed in classical Odù Ifá such as Ìrosùn Méjì and Òbàrà Méjì.
akunlegba_payload.etymology_and_philosophy: Compound noun: 'À' (that which) + 'kúnlẹ̀' (kneel) + 'gbà' (to receive or accept). It reflects the complementary dialectic of Yorùbá philosophy: humans have the freedom to choose (Àkúnlẹ̀yàn), but they must also receive and accept certain unalterable cosmic endowments (Àkúnlẹ̀gbà), such as biological parents, ancestral heritage, and natural lifespan.
akunlegba_payload.material_and_craftsmanship: Ritualized through offerings to the ancestral spirits (Ẹbọ Ìran) and the maintenance of personal balance through good character (Ìwà Pẹ̀lẹ́).
akunlegba_payload.social_and_court_protocol: Invoked to counsel humility, self-acceptance, and gratitude. Elders teach that when one recognizes one's Àkúnlẹ̀gbà, one ceases destructive envy and instead focuses on perfecting one's endowed talents.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Àkúnlẹ̀gbà kò ṣeé fọwọ́ pa rẹ́; ohun tí Ọlọ́run bá fi fúnni, a kì í fi agbára gba òmíràn. (That which was received kneeling cannot be rubbed out by human hands; what the Creator has bestowed cannot be violently exchanged for another's portion.)
Bí a kúnlẹ̀ gbà á, bẹ́ẹ̀ ni a gbọdọ̀ tẹ́wọ́ gbà á lórí ayé pẹ̀lú ìdùnnú. (As we knelt to receive it in heaven, so must we embrace it on earth with joyful gratitude.)
Àkúnlẹ̀gbà lẹ́wà; olúkálukú pẹ̀lú ẹ̀bùn tí Ọba Ọ̀run kọ́ fún un. (The received portion is beautiful; each soul carries the specific gifts fashioned for it by the King of Heaven.)
akunlegba_payload.diaspora_connections: Reflected in Afro-Cuban and Brazilian Candomblé traditions as the divine recognition of an initiate's natural spiritual faculties (Camino / Odù de Nacimiento).
akunlegba_payload.cinematic_and_media_production: Visuals of cupped open hands receiving water or glowing embers from an unseen celestial presence, framed against calm ancestral twilight.

sensory_aesthetics.tactile: Cool sensation of palm oil and shea butter (Òrí) applied during head propitiation.
sensory_aesthetics.auditory: Calm, reassuring voice of family matriarchs offering ancestral blessings.
sensory_aesthetics.visual: Open palms held upward in reverent reception.

akunlegba_payload.provenance_and_citations: Wándé Abímbọ́lá (1976), Ifá Literary Corpus; E.B. Ìdòwú (1962), Olódùmarè: God in Yoruba Belief; Rowland Abiodun (2014), Yoruba Art and Language.
